status: Draft; not published or validated assessment

sets.title: Connect the concern
sets.description: Match what is said with a question that opens the conversation.

items.prompt: Match each buyer statement to its most relevant clarifying question. These are possible next questions, not diagnoses.
pairs: What will your partner need to evaluate?
What changes for you in November?
I am unsure it fits our team.
Which part feels least relevant to your team?
items.feedback: You kept stakeholders, timing, and relevance separate instead of treating each as a request for a discount.
items.hint: Look for what you know, what you do not know, and what would clarify the decision.

items.prompt: Connect the observation to a useful follow-up.
pairs: Which implementation concern would you like to resolve?
Which criteria will you use to compare them?
The buyer says the price is high.
High compared with which option or expectation?
items.feedback: Each question checks a specific unknown. None assumes what the buyer secretly thinks.
items.hint: Look for what you know, what you do not know, and what would clarify the decision.

items.prompt: Connect the unsupported conclusion to the evidence still needed.
pairs: They laughed, so they will buy.
Their explicit decision and next step
They asked questions, so the offer fits.
They went quiet, so they dislike the price.
items.feedback: Engagement, curiosity, and silence are observations. Buying intent and fit require more evidence.
items.hint: Look for what you know, what you do not know, and what would clarify the decision.

sets.title: Choose the missing move
sets.description: A small word choice can change the whole question.

items.prompt: Before responding to an objection, first ____ what the person means.
items.feedback: Clarify first. A useful response depends on the actual concern, not the label you give it.
items.hint: Look for what you know, what you do not know, and what would clarify the decision.

items.prompt: Information describes an offer. Decision support connects it to the buyer’s ____.
items.feedback: Relevance comes from the buyer’s situation. More information alone does not establish fit.
items.hint: Look for what you know, what you do not know, and what would clarify the decision.

items.prompt: “Not yet” describes a skill still being developed; it is not proof of permanent ____.
items.feedback: An incomplete skill is a reason to prepare and practise, not to claim either expertise or permanent inability.
items.hint: Look for what you know, what you do not know, and what would clarify the decision.

sets.title: Build a better question
sets.description: Assemble a respectful follow-up, then understand why it works.

items.prompt: The buyer needs to talk with a partner. Build a question that supports that process.
items.feedback: This respects the buying process and helps the buyer prepare. It does not pressure them to exclude someone important.
items.hint: Look for what you know, what you do not know, and what would clarify the decision.

items.prompt: The buyer says “I need to think.” Build an invitation to clarify.
items.feedback: An open question creates room for the actual issue, including a genuine no.
items.hint: Look for what you know, what you do not know, and what would clarify the decision.

items.prompt: You have not handled this situation before. Build a responsible next-action statement.
items.feedback: Prepared action and feedback generate evidence. Confidence alone is not proof of competence.
items.hint: Look for what you know, what you do not know, and what would clarify the decision.

sets.title: Put the conversation in order
sets.description: Sequence the idea, without pretending all calls follow a script.

items.prompt: Order this teaching scaffold for responding to an unfamiliar concern.
items.feedback: This is a useful practice scaffold, not a mandatory script for every real conversation.
items.hint: Look for what you know, what you do not know, and what would clarify the decision.

items.prompt: Order a productive self-review.
pieces: Try the change in a new situation
items.feedback: Start with evidence, then select one correction and test it. Do not jump directly to a diagnosis of the buyer.
items.hint: Look for what you know, what you do not know, and what would clarify the decision.

items.prompt: Order a responsible next step when you do not know an answer.
pieces: Say what you can and cannot verify
Agree how to get the answer
items.feedback: Do not invent certainty. A transparent path to an answer protects trust.
items.hint: Look for what you know, what you do not know, and what would clarify the decision.

sets.title: Choose your next move
sets.description: Three plausible responses. One better question for this context.

items.prompt: A prospect says: “I like it, but my partner and I make these decisions together.” What is the most useful next move?
options: Ask what their partner needs to evaluate.
Offer a discount for deciding alone today.
Send every case study without asking.
items.feedback: Support the actual decision process. A stakeholder is not automatically an obstacle to overcome.
items.hint: Look for what you know, what you do not know, and what would clarify the decision.

items.prompt: A buyer says: “Our current setup meets our needs and we are not looking to change.” They decline more discussion. What next?
options: Respect the decision and close politely.
Keep sending proof until they reply.
items.feedback: A genuine no is a valid outcome. Ethical qualification is not failure.
items.hint: Look for what you know, what you do not know, and what would clarify the decision.

items.prompt: You quoted a price and the buyer pauses. You do not know why. What should you avoid?
options: Assuming the silence proves they cannot afford it.
items.feedback: Silence alone does not explain the buyer’s thoughts or finances. Ask without diagnosing.
items.hint: Look for what you know, what you do not know, and what would clarify the decision.

sets.title: Spot the assumption
sets.description: Notice where a conclusion goes beyond what was observed.

items.prompt: “They asked about features, therefore they are ready to sign.” Which part is not established?
items.feedback: Curiosity does not establish commitment. Ask about decision criteria and the next step.
items.hint: Look for what you know, what you do not know, and what would clarify the decision.

items.prompt: “I explained everything, so they must understand.” What is missing?
items.feedback: Your explanation and their understanding are different. Invite the buyer to describe how the offer relates to their situation.
items.hint: Look for what you know, what you do not know, and what would clarify the decision.

items.prompt: “I have never closed this deal size; therefore I am incapable.” Which statement is a prediction rather than an observed fact?
options: I have no prior deal of that size.
I can prepare for a first attempt.
items.feedback: Past experience does not establish permanent inability. Prepare within your actual competence and seek feedback.
items.hint: Look for what you know, what you do not know, and what would clarify the decision.

sets.title: Listen before you solve
sets.description: Replay a fictional buyer line. The transcript is always available.

items.prompt: Listen to the buyer, then choose a relevant follow-up.
items.spoken: I am not sure how we would introduce this to our team.
options: What part of introducing it feels most uncertain?
items.feedback: The concern is about implementation in this statement. Explore it before introducing unrelated proof or pricing.
items.hint: Look for what you know, what you do not know, and what would clarify the decision.

items.prompt: Listen to the buyer. Which assumption should you avoid?
items.spoken: Let me discuss it with our operations head.
options: The buyer is definitely avoiding you.
items.feedback: An additional stakeholder can be a normal part of the process. Do not infer avoidance from this line alone.
items.hint: Look for what you know, what you do not know, and what would clarify the decision.

items.prompt: Listen, then identify a useful next move.
items.spoken: Thank you. This is not something we want to pursue.
options: Ignore the no and pitch again.
Acknowledge the decision and end respectfully.
items.feedback: Respect a clear no. Do not train persistence that overrides the person’s stated decision.
items.hint: Look for what you know, what you do not know, and what would clarify the decision.

sets.title: The branching conversation
sets.description: A small conversation with consequences, recovery, and a respectful exit.

items.prompt: A partner joins the decision

options.text: Ask what they need to evaluate.
Offer a special price if the buyer decides alone.

repair.buyer: That does not address what I said.

options.text: Acknowledge the mismatch and ask permission to clarify.

clarified.buyer: They are mainly worried about disruption.

options.text: Ask which part of implementation feels most disruptive.
Repeat the feature list without addressing this information.

repair2.buyer: Please respond to the concern I just described.

options.text: Ask which part of implementation feels most disruptive.

items.feedback: The next question follows the new information rather than repeating the pitch.
items.hint: Look for what you know, what you do not know, and what would clarify the decision.

items.prompt: Separate timing from relevance

options.text: Ask what changes after this month.

repair.buyer: That does not address what I said.

options.text: Acknowledge the mismatch and ask permission to clarify.

clarified.buyer: Our team is migrating systems until October.

options.text: Ask whether a later review would be useful and agree a date only with consent.
Repeat the feature list without addressing this information.

repair2.buyer: Please respond to the concern I just described.

options.text: Ask whether a later review would be useful and agree a date only with consent.

items.feedback: A timing constraint is not proof of poor interest or a price problem.
items.hint: Look for what you know, what you do not know, and what would clarify the decision.

items.prompt: Recognize when to stop

start.buyer: It does not address the issue we are working on.

options.text: Ask permission to clarify the mismatch.
Insist that every company needs this.

repair.buyer: That does not address what I said.

options.text: Acknowledge the mismatch and ask permission to clarify.

clarified.buyer: We are not interested in discussing it further.

options.text: Repeat the feature list without addressing this information.

repair2.buyer: Please respond to the concern I just described.

items.feedback: The branch can end without a sale and still demonstrate a good decision.
items.hint: Look for what you know, what you do not know, and what would clarify the decision.
